outcome: Residents' exposure to obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) repair
cohort: The study cohort comprised OBGYN residents' surgical experiences and 103,234 deliveries (vaginal and cesarean) from a community academic hospital over a 16-year period (2007-2022).
finding: Average resident exposure to obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) repair decreased from 11 (2007-2010) to 5 (2019-2022) during 4 years of training, with an overall average of 7 repairs (6 third-degree, 1 fourth-degree) per resident.
